questions.question: In a monohybrid cross between two heterozygous (Rr) pea plants for seed shape, where 'R' is dominant for round seeds and 'r' is recessive for wrinkled seeds, what will be the phenotypic ratio of round to wrinkled seeds in the F1 generation?

options.explanation: This is not the correct phenotypic ratio.
This is the correct phenotypic ratio.
This is not the correct phenotypic ratio.
This is not the correct phenotypic ratio.

questions.explanation: When two heterozygous (Rr) parents are crossed (Rr x Rr), the possible genotypes are RR, Rr, rR, and rr. This gives a genotypic ratio of 1 RR : 2 Rr : 1 rr. Since 'R' (round) is dominant over 'r' (wrinkled), both RR and Rr genotypes will express the round phenotype. questions.question: What determines the sex of a human child?

questions.explanation: Human females have two X chromosomes (XX), and males have one X and one Y chromosome (XY). All eggs produced by the mother carry an X chromosome.
